title: Wide-field Fluorescent Microscopy and Fluorescent Imaging Flow Cytometry on a Cell-phone
protocol: Place the lens into the attachment within its specific lens holder position.
Place the plastic filter onto the filter tray and slide it into the attachment; or tape the plastic filter in front of the cell-phone camera lens.
Insert the LED tray into the attachment.
Place the sample glass slides into the sample tray.
Slide the sample tray into the attachment.
Face the LEDs toward the sample.
Clip the attachment onto the cell-phone, such that the extra lens is directly in touch with the cell-phone camera lens.
Use the switch on the attachment to turn on the LEDs.
Image the sample of interest with the cell-phone camera unit using its "night mode".
Place the aspherical lens into the attachment.
Place the plastic filter onto the filter tray and slide it into the attachment; or tape the plastic filter in front of the cellphone camera lens.
Slide the microfluidic channel into the same opto-fluidic attachment.
Clip the attachment onto the cell-phone such that the extra lens is directly in touch with the cell-phone camera lens.
Use the switch on the attachment to turn on the LEDs.
Connect the microfluidic channel to the syringe pump and deliver the liquid sample into the microfluidic device at a constant flow rate.
Capture a movie of the fluorescent cells/particles flowing through the microfluidic channel using the video mode of the cell-phone camera.
Mix 10 μl of green fluorescent beads with 40 μl of DI water.
Mix 10 μl of red fluorescent beads with 40 μl of DI water from the previous step.
Place 10 μl of the bead mixture on a glass slide using a micropipette.
Put another glass slide on top of the bead mixture to create a sandwich structure.
Insert the sandwich structure into the sample tray and slide it into the cell-phone attachment.
Take SYTO16 nucleic acid fluorescent labeling kit out from the refrigerator and bring it to room temperature.
Transfer 200 μl whole blood sample from an EDTA blood collection tube to a 1.5 ml polystyrene tube.
Add 1 ml red blood cell lysing buffer to the 200 μl whole blood sample and mix thoroughly.
Centrifuge the lysed blood sample for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant solution after centrifugation.
Resuspend the white blood cell pellet into 200 μl PBS buffer and gently mix them.
Add 5 μl of 1 mM SYTO16 solution to the white blood cell sample.
Wrap the sample with aluminum foil.
Incubate the wrapped sample in a dark environment for approximately 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample again.
Remove the supernatant.
Re-suspend the labeled white blood cell pellet in PBS buffer.
Place 5-10 μl of labeled white blood cell liquid sample on a cover slip.
Place a second cover slip on top of the sample.
Insert the sandwiched sample slide into the sample tray.
Image the sample using the cell-phone fluorescent microscope.
Alternatively, deliver the fluorescently labeled white blood cells through a microfluidic channel using an automated syringe pump.
Capture a fluorescent microscopic movie of the flowing cells using the cell-phone camera in video mode.
